title: Dotmesh usage metrics for backend
body:
In order to understand what our SaaS users doing we want to track all their dm usage against our dotmesh cluster.

Things to note:
 * Consider this in our GDPR consent!
 * Monitor the tracking data

We want to know when users have:
* Installed it 
* Pushed/pulled etc
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Also, in _our_ backend we want to push every event that happens into Segment (every RPC and push/pull probably). Not a problem if this code gets shipped to our users too, as long as it's disabled by default.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: To clarify,   interactions with _our_ datamesh server backend should track _all_ actions (not just the 4-hourly “i’m this version” ping) and which authenticated users initiated the request so that we can track backend events in the same manner that we track frontend events in segment

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: We will forward events to segment so this issue involves plugging in the golang segment api client

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: I'm concerned that as the SaaS takes off, this will become a lot of work to hammer the Segment APIs. I'm assuming they won't rate-limit us, but if I'm to look into batching pings, or putting them into a local queue and having a pool of processes feeding them up to Segment, can I just confirm that it's OK if events are delayed sometimes (hours at worst) in the name of making the system more scaleable and fault-tolerant?

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
The implementation of this is being split into a few different items, so I'm closing this issue:

 - https://github.com/dotmesh-io/marketing-site/issues/49 to get customer IDs from the marketing site into the SaaS UI
 -  https://github.com/dotmesh-io/dothub/issues/32 to get customer IDs from the SaaS UI into the SaaS core
 - #286 to log API calls against that customer ID.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
